newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian tycoon says to focus on charity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian tycoon says to focus on charity.

text.p: Indonesian tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hassan said on Tuesday he wants to transform the Nusamba group, which has stakes in the rich Busang gold property and the country's top car maker, into a huge charitable body.
Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto, and 10 percent each by Hasan and Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto.

The group owns an 8.26-percent-share of Indonesia's top car maker, Astra International, and last week landed an enviable stake in the huge Busang gold find in East Kalimantan which has deposits currently worth $24 billion.
"We want to be like the Rockefeller or Ford foundations," Hasan told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"I have enough (money). I can only eat three times a day, and play 45 holes (of golf) a day," said the diminutive Hasan, a regular golfing partner of Suharto.

He said Nusamba, of which he is group chairman, had revised its investment policy, no longer wanting to depend merely on public donations and use interest from bank deposits to finance its operations.
"We thought that if we had shares...10, 20, 30 percent, these shares will be of greater value instead of having the money...it's better than money," he said.
"As a result we now have 150 companies," he said. "One of them is the largest insurance company in Indonesia."
Sports lover Hasan, a youthful-looking 65, forged a close relationship with Suharto during the 1950s when the president was regional military commander in central Java.

Hasan is also president commissioner of Bank Umum Nasional, private banks Bank Bukopin and Bank Duta and paper maker PT Kiani Kertas. He is also a commissioner of insurance company PT Tugu Pratama Indonesia.
The Nusamba group announced plans late last month to buy the 49 percent stake in PT Indocopper Investama held by conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers for $311.8 million.

Indocopper has 9.36 percent of PT Freeport Indonesia, which runs one of the world's largest copper and gold mines in Irian Jaya province. Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc has an 81.28-percent-stake in Freeport Indonesia.
"Nusamba is going to be more aggressive so that when we are not around any more, we can still help the unfortunate," he said. "My main business is helping the unfortunate."
Hasan said Nusamba was building a $1.1-billion-pulp mill in East Kalimantan with funds raised through local syndication, and was offering $20 million annually in student scholarships.
"We have sponsored 40,000 university graduates over the past 20 years and are helping 1,200 institutions assisting the blind, crippled children and orphans," he said.
"We are building a $60-million-cancer hospital and are planning to set up clinics in some 300 regencies," he said.

Hasan's corporate profile has been raised significantly since Nusamba's entry into Busang after spending most of his life in the timber business, where he heads a cartel of Indonesian plywood producers.
"It's about the same. Before it was green gold, now it's real gold," he said.
